subject: Technical validation: NimbusOps connector - architecture review & test plan
content:
From: Samantha Park <samantha@nimbusops.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: NimbusOps - Redwood connector: initial reference design

Hi Marissa / Rohan / Rafael,

Thanks again for the time today. As promised, attaching a first-cut reference diagram for the Redwood connector and a short compatibility checklist. High-level notes:

- Our approach is to place a lightweight NimbusOps adapter in front of the Redwood Hosted API to handle schema translation, retry/backoff policies, and tokenization normalization.
- We recommend a pooled adapter deployment per region (us-east1 / us-west1) to keep RTT low.
- Sensitive PII fields should be redacted at the adapter layer before forwarding to Redwood unless customer explicitly opts-in.

Attachments: nimbusops-reference-design-v1.png, compatibility-test-matrix.csv

Next steps we propose:
1) Confirm required API surfaces (streaming vs non-streaming)
2) Sync up on auth pattern (service-account JWTs vs mTLS)
3) Run a short lab test against a Canary model to validate KV cache behavior under prefix-heavy traffic

Would love to schedule an architecture review tomorrow if that works for the team.

Best,
Samantha Park
Senior Solutions Architect
NimbusOps

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Park <samantha@nimbusops.io>
Cc: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NimbusOps - Redwood connector: initial reference design

Samantha — thanks for the file. The diagram looks sensible; two quick clarifications before we lock in an architecture review:

1) Auth: we prefer short-lived JWTs (Redwood-managed) for hosted customers; for Dedicated/Private customers we will support mTLS. Can you confirm whether NimbusOps can issue and rotate client certs for private deployments?

2) Caching semantics: we need the adapter to preserve Redwood KV cache keys or we risk cache fragmentation. Can you confirm you can carry through the raw prompt prefix unmodified (aside from PII redaction)?

Evelyn, can you weigh in on the monitoring signals we should ask NimbusOps to emit (latency p50/p95, token counts, cache hit ratio)?

If tomorrow works for everyone, I can book a 60-minute slot and share an agenda.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Head of Partner Integrations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0194

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Samantha Park <samantha@nimbusops.io>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NimbusOps - Redwood connector: initial reference design

Looks good. Two items to call out from an infra perspective:

- Rate limiting/fan-out: if a single NimbusOps adapter receives high concurrency we need a plan for backpressure. Suggest we test steady-state 400 RPS with 512 token average and a 100ms target p95.
- Fallbacks: define a graceful degradation for when Redwood Dedicated capacity is saturated (route to a lower-cost hosted model or queue with opaque 202).

Evelyn — monitoring signals: p50/p95 latency, requests/sec, tokens/sec, KV cache hit ratio, adapter errors (4xx/5xx), and end-to-end request id tracing. Ideally export with OpenTelemetry.

I'll add the test scenarios to INF-4321 after the call.

-Rohan

Thanks — adding monitoring checklist here:
- p50/p95 latency (in ms) per region
- tokens-in / tokens-out per request type
- KV cache hit ratio (per model)
- adapter CPU / memory per pod
- percent redaction events (count of PII redactions)
- OpenTelemetry span IDs propagated from adapter -> Redwood runtime

Samantha: can you add example traces for a streaming session and a non-streaming generate to the Drive link? That will help validate our tracing ingestion.

Evelyn
Director, Product Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Park <samantha@nimbusops.io>

Cc: NimbusOps Solutions <partner-arch@nimbusops.io>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NimbusOps - Redwood connector: initial reference design

Marissa / team —

Great feedback. Quick responses inline:
- mTLS: yes, NimbusOps supports automated cert issuance and rotation for customer-controlled CA; we can also support short-lived JWTs for hosted customers.
- KV key preservation: we can pass the raw prefix through an encrypted header and only redact the PII payload fields; config flag to disable any prefix transformation.
- Backpressure: adapter supports token-based throttling and can return Retry-After headers; we'll include a 202-style queue option as part of the integration.

I've uploaded two example traces (streaming + non-streaming) and an updated diagram to the Drive folder you shared. Also attached a short CSV with our preliminary lab test results against a small Redwood canary model.

Attachments: compatibility-test-matrix.csv, nimbusops-reference-design-v1.png

Would 10am PT tomorrow for an architecture review work for you? If so, share an agenda and I'll invite our Solution Engineering lead.

Best,
Samantha
